method: The layout is a lattice of square blocks turned 45 degrees, so a block set on point is as wide as its diagonal, the finished block size times the square root of 2. Side setting triangles fill the gaps between the block points along the four edges and are cut as quarter-square triangles: a square of the diagonal plus five seam allowances, cut twice on the diagonal, gives four side triangles. At a quarter-inch seam that addition is 1 1/4 inches, the figure Quilter's Cache and Quiltville print. The four corner triangles are half-square triangles from a square of the diagonal divided by the root of two plus three and a half seam allowances, which is block / 1.414 + 7/8 inch at a quarter-inch seam, cut once on the diagonal for two. Both cut sizes are rounded up to the next 1/8 inch, or to the next whole millimetre in metric mode; the unrounded value is reported beside them. The layout needs two side triangles for each gap along the top and bottom and down each side, so 2 x (across - 1) + 2 x (down - 1), and always four corner triangles from two squares, so cutting whole squares can leave spares. The blocks themselves fill both grids, so the setting holds across x down + (across - 1) x (down - 1) blocks, and the finished centre measures across x block x root 2 by down x block x root 2 before any border. Ranges are 0.25 to 60 inches (0.635 to 152.4 centimetres) for the block, 0.1 to 1 inch (0.254 to 2.54 centimetres) for the seam allowance and 1 to 25 blocks each way; a missing, non-numeric, four-decimal or out-of-range value, a fractional block count and an unknown unit are each refused with a message naming the field. Conversions use exactly 2.54 centimetres per inch. Cutting the side squares twice leaves the straight grain on the long outside edge and cutting the corner squares once leaves it on the short edges at the corners, which is why the two are cut differently. Sashing, borders, backing, binding and fabric yardage are not modelled, and the top is trimmed 1/4 inch beyond the outermost points once sewn. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Quilter's Cache - "Setting Triangles": the corner square is the finished block divided by 1.414 plus 7/8 inch and the side square is the finished block times 1.414 plus 1 1/4 inches, both rounded up to the nearest 1/8 inch

QuiltLab - "How to Set Quilt Blocks on Point": the same side and corner formulas, four side triangles from a square cut on both diagonals and two corner triangles from a square cut once, with the 12 inch worked figures of 18 1/4 and 9 3/8 inches
